role: Template for a local .env of overrides (SCHEME, PROJECT, MIN_COVERAGE, DESTINATION) intended for scripts/run_tests_with_coverage.sh.
toplevel: Data only. Lines 1-10: SCHEME=Emuqu, PROJECT=Emuqu.xcodeproj; comments say coverage floors live in .ci/min_coverage.txt and .ci/min_coverage_logic.txt and MIN_COVERAGE overrides the overall floor; optional DESTINATION=id=<simulator-id>. .gitignore:126-128 ignores .env/.env.local/.env.*.local. No file in the repo sources or reads a .env file: scripts/run_tests_with_coverage.sh:6-9 only reads already-exported environment variables (SCHEME/PROJECT/RESULT_BUNDLE/MIN_COVERAGE with defaults), and scripts/lib/preflight.sh contains no env loading; so a copied .env has no effect unless the user exports it into the shell themselves. Correction: scripts/run_tests_with_coverage.sh also honours an exported DESTINATION (line 53-56, otherwise select_simulator_destination.sh). The commented example MIN_COVERAGE=16 is far below the committed floors (.ci/min_coverage.txt = 44, .ci/min_coverage_logic.txt = 45) and equals the hard-coded fallback in scripts/check_coverage.sh:48.

flags.text: The file presents itself as 'Optional local overrides for scripts/run_tests_with_coverage.sh', but no script, Makefile target or hook loads a .env file (grep for source/.env/dotenv finds nothing); values put in .env are silently ignored unless exported manually.

The template's example MIN_COVERAGE=16 is the stale fallback value (check_coverage.sh:48), not the committed overall floor of 44; a developer who uncomments and exports it lowers the coverage gate from 44% to 16% for their runs.
